scope: All original acceptance/evidence criteria for issues #4 and #10; milestone production/deployment gates remain separate and open.

criteria.original_requirement: Specify non-forgeable resource authority for database namespaces, filesystem operations and network origins.
criteria.assessment: Host-issued DB/file/origin authority is not a GoPyT value; forged host scope values are rejected.

criteria.original_requirement: Define grant attenuation, delegation, revocation and in-flight operation behavior; applications cannot widen their own authority.
criteria.assessment: Delegation only attenuates, ancestors revoke descendants, expiry is monotonic, and admitted operations may finish.

criteria.original_requirement: Enforce authority consistently across transitive calls, native boundaries, caches and concurrent tasks.
criteria.assessment: VM/native admission covers transitive calls, cached reads, atomic batches, parallel children and HTTP workers.

criteria.original_requirement: Test cross-tenant access, confused-deputy cases, policy changes, traversal/link races and mixed-authority atomic batches.
criteria.assessment: Real HTTP verifies distinct bearer principals and mixed-tenant batch denial; resource regressions cover deputies, policy changes and file replacement after admission.

criteria.original_requirement: Retain reviewed design decisions, implementation references, meaningful regression/end-to-end tests, and failure evidence appropriate to this scope.
criteria.assessment: Reviewed native/thread/audience decisions, implementation references, regressions and unsuccessful fixture/environment trials are retained. This is not an independent security audit.

criteria.original_requirement: For performance/data claims, freeze workload/source identities before tuning, compare with an independent oracle, and report actual limits and unsuccessful trials.
criteria.assessment: No performance/SLO or real-data-campaign claim is made. Regression sources/fixtures are frozen, fixed expected tenant results are asserted independently of permission lookup, and failures/limits are retained.

criteria.original_requirement: Update user-facing documentation and the architecture tracker; do not equate finite passing tests with universal correctness or security.
criteria.assessment: User-facing security/architecture documents define supported behavior and limits. Remote tracker/issue publication must be verified after merge; finite tests do not imply universal security.

criteria.original_requirement: Define verified request identity, tenant context and authorization policy interfaces with least privilege and deny-by-default behavior.
criteria.assessment: Broker-issued opaque sessions carry immutable verified subject/tenant context, deny omitted rights, and reject mismatched module/VM audiences.

criteria.original_requirement: Bind authorization to the resource operation and authenticated identity, never to an unverified client-supplied tenant identifier.
criteria.assessment: A credential selects host-provisioned tenant grants; header/body/URL tenant claims cannot widen them. Every native resource admission checks the session authority.

criteria.original_requirement: Specify provisioning, revocation, token/session expiry and supported gateway or identity-provider integration, including MFA responsibilities.
criteria.assessment: Operator provisioning, revocation/replacement, one-hour bounded monotonic sessions and the strict TLS-gateway credential contract are specified. Upstream human authentication/MFA is an explicit trusted-host responsibility; no OAuth/JWT validation is claimed.

criteria.original_requirement: Test cross-tenant reads/writes, privilege escalation, stale credentials, batch authorization and concurrent policy changes through real HTTP.
criteria.assessment: Real HTTP and encrypted strict-profile tests verify cross-tenant reads/writes, route escalation, stale credentials, atomic batches, reused connections, and concurrent policy changes.

criteria.original_requirement: Retain reviewed design decisions, implementation references, meaningful regression/end-to-end tests, and failure evidence appropriate to this scope.
criteria.assessment: Reviewed native/thread/audience decisions, implementation references, regressions and unsuccessful fixture/environment trials are retained. This is not an independent security audit.

criteria.original_requirement: For performance/data claims, freeze workload/source identities before tuning, compare with an independent oracle, and report actual limits and unsuccessful trials.
criteria.assessment: No performance/SLO or real-data-campaign claim is made. Regression sources/fixtures are frozen, fixed expected tenant results are asserted independently of permission lookup, and failures/limits are retained.

criteria.original_requirement: Update user-facing documentation and the architecture tracker; do not equate finite passing tests with universal correctness or security.
criteria.assessment: User-facing security/architecture documents define supported behavior and limits. Remote tracker/issue publication must be verified after merge; finite tests do not imply universal security.

publication_gates: Merge implementation with passing supported-platform CI at the final head.
Publish current evidence on both issues and update the architecture parent.
Verify remote body/checklist/state changes before treating issue closure as complete.
limitations: Trusted Python host; no protection from hostile Python in the same process.
Supported authentication mode is operator-provisioned opaque bearer sessions; upstream human MFA/IdP verification belongs to the trusted host integration.
No deployed TLS/gateway/MFA/IdP security qualification or independent audit claimed.
No throughput, beyond-RAM, SLO, recovery or universal safety claim.
